# Adjudication Task — Chapter 727

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃727화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|찢을까, 말까.
  6|
  7|얼굴 위로 생각이 고스란히 드러난 진태경을 바라보며, 최민우는 내심 어이없는 실소를 흘렸다.
  8|
  9|‘도무지 알 수가 없단 말이지.’
 10|
 11|평소 보이는 언행도, 생각도 단순하기 그지없다.
 12|
 13|하지만 가끔 진태경이 보여 주는 어떤 면모는, 놀랍다 못해 경악스러울 정도였다.
 14|
 15|‘더 놀라는 것도 이상하지만, 그래도 이건 정말이지…….’
 16|
 17|최민우의 시선이 테이블 위에 머물렀다.
 18|
 19|[싱글벙글 마나 연공법]
 20|
 21|어린아이가 쓴 것처럼 삐뚤빼뚤한 글씨체와 우습기 그지없는 제목.
 22|
 23|그러나 저 열 장 남짓한 A4용지에 담긴 내용은, 제목과 달리 결코 우습지 않았다.
 24|
 25|‘아예 새로운 마나 연공법을 만들다니.’
 26|
 27|앞서 최민우가 악필까지 지적해 가며 진태경은 골려 준 이유는 간단했다.
 28|
 29|이처럼 말도 안 되는 물건을 갑작스럽게, 그것도 한마디 말도 없이 전한 것에 대한 소소한 복수,
 30|
 31|몇 시간 전, 최민우가 느꼈던 충격은 그만큼 엄청난 것이었다.
 32|
 33|‘어떻게 이럴 수 있지?’
 34|
 35|지금껏 본 적 없는 간단명료한 설명과 방식. 더없이 안정적이며, 기본기에 충실한 마나 연공법.
 36|
 37|그리고 어느덧 무림의 절정 고수와 비교해도 뒤떨어지지 않는 실력자가 된 최민우는, 이 새로운 마나 연공법의 진가를 즉각 알아차릴 수 있었다.
 38|
 39|더불어 불과 얼마 전, 세상의 이목을 끌었던 일련의 사건이 진태경에게 어떤 의미였는지도.
 40|
 41|“심판의 일주일.”
 42|
 43|짧은 침묵을 깨트린 최민우가 진태경을 응시하며 말을 이었다.
 44|
 45|“마치 신께서 일주일에 걸쳐 천지를 창조했던 것처럼, 전 세계의 테러리스트들은 심판의 일주일을 보냈다. 며칠 전 도람프 주니어 미 대통령이 백악관 기자회견에서 한 말입니다.”
 46|
 47|다른 누구도 아닌 미국 대통령이 공식 석상에서 한 발언이다.
 48|
 49|당연하게도 그의 파격적인 언행은 불과 한 시간이 지나기도 전에 일파만파 퍼져 나갔고, 어느 정도 시간이 흐른 지금은 대한민국에서도 모르는 사람이 없다.
 50|
 51|아마도 한 사람을 제외한다면.
 52|
 53|“그 양반이 그런 말을 했어요?”
 54|
 55|줄곧 트레이닝 룸에만 처박혀 있던 진태경의 물음에, 최민우가 고개를 끄덕였다.
 56|
 57|“한 나라의, 그것도 미국 대통령의 발언치고는 꽤 과격했습니다. 테러리스트들을 일부러 자극한다는 비판도 있었고요.”
 58|
 59|“흠. 뭘 또 거창하게 천지창조씩이나. 그래서 보복성 테러는요?”
 60|
 61|“없었습니다. 단 한 건도.”
 62|
 63|“단 한 건도?”
 64|
 65|“네. 오히려 말을 아끼기까지 하더군요.”
 66|
 67|아직도 뚱해 있던 진태경의 표정이 살짝 풀렸다.
 68|
 69|“열심히 두들겨 팬 보람이 있네.”
 70|
 71|바로 그 순간이었다.
 72|
 73|진태경을 물끄러미 바라보던 최민우가 불쑥 입을 연 것은.
 74|
 75|“그래서였군요.”
 76|
 77|“뭐가요?”
 78|
 79|“두 가지에 대해 생각해 봤습니다. 갑자기 테러리스트를 진압하신 이유. 또 이 새로운 마나 연공법을 제게 주신 의미에 대해서.”
 80|
 81|그리고 답이 나왔다.
 82|
 83|[싱글벙글 마나 연공법].
 84|
 85|도무지 성의라고는 찾아볼 수 없는 호치케스 한 방으로 묶인 그것을 들어 올리며, 최민우가 말을 이었다.
 86|
 87|“모든 사람들에게 공개할 생각이시군요. 이 마나 연공법을.”
 88|
 89|진태경이 씩 웃었다.
 90|
 91|“우리 최 팀장님, 역시 똑똑하시다니까.”
 92|
 93|
 94|
 95|* * *
 96|
 97|
 98|
 99|지금 이 순간, 나를 바라보는 최 팀장의 표정은 오묘했다.
100|
101|감탄하는 것 같기도 하고, 한편으로는 여러모로 생각이 많아진 것 같기도 했다.
102|
103|“왜요, 무슨 문제라도?”
104|
105|“글쎄요.”
106|
107|최 팀장이 헝클어진 머리를 매만졌다.
108|
109|“너무 많은 문제가 있어서 뭐부터 말씀드려야 할지 모르겠습니다.”
110|
111|“제가 만든 마나 연공법에는 문제가 없으니, 현실적인 부분이겠네요.”
112|
113|“……예, 안타깝게도 그렇습니다.”
114|
115|“그중에서 어떤 게 가장 큰 문젭니까?”
116|
117|잠시 생각하던 최 팀장이 입을 열었다.
118|
119|“우선 이 마나 연공법을 공개한다는 것만으로도 첫 번째 문제가 되겠죠.”
120|
121|“계속 말씀하세요.”
122|
123|“마나 연공법은 상위 헌터들 중에서도 극소수만이 보유한, 일종의 노하우이자 비전이라는 사실은 진태경 씨도 잘 알고 계실 겁니다. 그들이 얼마나 폐쇄적인지, 또 그들이 속한 세계가 여타의 헌터들과는 얼마나 다른지에 대해서도요.”
124|
125|“알죠. 이 바닥에서 구른 게 몇 년인데. 물론 F급 헌터 시절에는 마나 연공법에 대해 들어 본 적도 없지만.”
126|
127|세상에 존재하는 어떤 직업보다 격차가 심한 것이 헌터다.
128|
129|일반적인 사회인들이 학력과 집안, 외모로 서로를 구별한다면, 헌터는 오직 등급에 따라 귀천(貴賤)이 갈린다.
130|
131|얼마나 많은 마나를 부여받았는지. 얼마나 민첩하고 힘이 강한지. 그런 원초적인 기준에 따라 선별되고 곧 도축당할 소처럼 등급이 매겨지는 거다.
132|
133|‘괜히 F급 헌터를 노비라고 부르는 게 아니지.’
134|
135|반면 상위 헌터들은 그야말로 구름 위의 존재나 다름없다.
136|
137|그들은 어지간한 헌터가 평생 일해도 벌 수 없는 금액을 레이드 한 번으로 벌어들이고, 부러움이 담긴 시선과 스포트라이트 속에서 살아간다.
138|
139|아마 그래서일 것이다.
140|
141|과거 귀족들이 성을 짓고 살아가던 것처럼, 그들 역시 자신들만을 위한 벽을 지었다.
142|
143|상위 헌터가 아니라면 누구도 넘을 수 없는 벽.
144|
145|설령 운이 좋은 누군가가 높은 등급을 받았더라도, 자신들의 허락이 있어야만 열리는 문까지.
146|
147|그렇게 보이지 않는 끈으로 연결된 상위 헌터들은 전 세계에 퍼져 있고, 그들은 저마다 속한 거대 길드들의 비호를 받는다.
148|
149|“이건 단지 국내에만 한정된 문제가 아닙니다. 이 마나 연공법을 세상에 공개하면, 예상하는 것 이상으로 엄청난 반발이 일어날 겁니다.”
150|
151|“우리 쪽에서 마나 연공법을 까면, 자신들이 지닌 가치가 떨어진다고 생각할 테니까?”
152|
153|“그것도 그렇지만, 한 가지 이유가 더 있습니다.”
154|
155|“뭔데요?”
156|
157|“바로 ‘우리’라서 문제인 겁니다.”
158|
159|“……!”
160|
161|짤막한 대답이었지만, 나는 그 말이 뜻하는 바를 즉각 깨달았다.
162|
163|‘그간 너무 튀었나.’
164|
165|문득 로그아웃하기 직전 적천강과 나누었던 대화가 생각난다.
166|
167|원했든, 원치 않았든 이미 필요 이상으로 많은 주목을 받았다는 그의 한 마디가.
168|
169|스포트라이트는 밝다. 하지만 그 주위는 어둡다.
170|
171|학창 시절 좋아하던 어느 소설에서 읽었던 그 글귀가 맞았다. 내가 밝아지는 만큼, 나를 둘러싼 어둠 역시 짙어지고 있었다.
172|
173|무림에서도. 그리고 현대에서도.
174|
175|“최 팀장님, 혹시?”
176|
177|내가 무엇을 묻는지 알아차린 최 팀장이 고개를 저었다.
178|
179|“아직 큰 문제는 없습니다만…… 보이지 않는 압박이 들어오고 있습니다. 그래서 해외 지사의 추가 설립도 잠시 보류하고 있고요.”
180|
181|“그 정도예요?”
182|
183|“당장 전 세계의 모든 거대 길드가 우리를 주시하고 있습니다. 꼭 무력시위가 아니더라도 그들이 어떻게든 손을 쓴다면, 저희로서도 상황이 쉽지 않습니다.”
184|
185|“아니, 왜 말씀 안 하셨어요?”
186|
187|최 팀장이 정색하며 대답했다.
188|
189|“말할 틈이나 줬습니까?”
190|
191|“……그건 그러네.”
192|
193|그나저나 이 동네도 개판이구만.
194|
195|본래 가진 것이 많은 이들은 세상이 변화하는 것을 꺼린다.
196|
197|독자적인 마나 연공법을 익힌 극소수의 헌터들 역시 그 범주를 벗어나지 못한다.
198|
199|‘아니, 사실 이쯤 되면 헌터보다는 권력자라고 하는 게 맞겠지.’
200|
201|어쩌면 한 나라를 주무를 수 있는 권력자들.
202|
203|막대한 부와 명예, 그리고 압도적인 힘으로 상식마저 뒤엎는 그들은 더 이상의 변화도. 자신들과 비견할 만한 또 다른 권력자의 등장도 원치 않는다.
204|
205|이를테면, 나나 최 팀장이라든지.
206|
207|‘아무리 그래도 그렇지. 이 새끼들은 무림 문파보다 한술 더 뜨는 것 같은데.’
208|
209|독문 무공이 유출되면 눈에 불을 켜고 쫓아가 뚝배기를 깨 버리는 곳이 무림이라지만, 적어도 시장에서 삼재검법을 파는 상인한테 지랄발광을 떨지는 않는다.
210|
211|그런데 가진 것도 많은 놈들이, 소소하게 마나 연공법 하나 풀려고 하니까 지랄하려고 하네?
212|
213|어? 열 받네?
214|
215|“이 마나 연공법 까면, 걔들 난리나겠죠?”
216|
217|“네. 저희도 난리 나고요.”
218|
219|“그럼 제가 걔들을 까면요?”
220|
221|“네?”
222|
223|“생각해 보니까 좆 같잖아요. 그냥 무지성으로 마나 연공법부터 까 보고, 그 후에 지랄하는 새끼들도 까면 조용해질…….”
224|
225|“안 돼! 하지 마! 절대!”
226|
227|늘 낮고 침착한 최 팀장의 목소리가 이 정도 데시벨을 낸다는 것은, ‘차라리 내 시체를 밟고 가라, 이 미친 새끼야.’라는 뜻이다.
228|
229|하지만 이번만큼은 나도 쉽게 수긍할 수 없었다.
230|
231|“최 팀장님 뜻은 알겠는데, 이건 공개해야 합니다. 일기장처럼 혼자 간직하려고 만든 거 아니에요.”
232|
233|이미 전 세계적으로 마력이 증가했다. 아니, 지금 이 순간에도 증가하고 있다.
234|
235|그로 인해 변이 게이트가 속출하고 이제는 몬스터 웨이브까지 일어나는 판국이었다.
236|
237|“마력이 증가하는 만큼 몬스터도 강해지고 있습니다. 팀장님도 아시잖아요. 하지만 현재 상황에서 이 마나 연공법이 사람들에게 알려진다면…….”
238|
239|“헌터들의 전체적인 수준이 높아지겠죠. 최하급 헌터도 무리 없이 익힐 수 있을 만큼 안정성이 뛰어나니까요.”
240|
241|최 팀장이 굳은 얼굴로 말을 이었다.
242|
243|“진태경 씨께서 무슨 생각이신지는 압니다. 애초부터 여러 반군 집단과 테러리스트들을 진압하신 이유도, 마나 연공법이 악용될 가능성을 최대한 줄이기 위해서가 아닙니까?”
244|
245|“네. 제가 만든 무기의 예리함보다는, 우선 누구의 손에 들어갈 것인지를 따져 봐야 했으니까.”
246|
247|현대의 시간으로 약 2주 전, 미국 텍사스에서 벌어진 한 가지 사건은 내게 경각심을 심어 주었다.
248|
249|다름 아닌 마정석을 이용한 테러.
250|
251|다행히 테러범의 시도는 수포로 돌아갔고 어떠한 사상자도 발생하지 않았지만, 나는 그 사건으로 인해 확실히 깨달았다.
252|
253|“제가 생각하고 있는 ‘모두’라는 단어에는, 온갖 범죄자와 미치광이들까지 포함되어 있더라고요.”
254|
255|이후 매직 존슨을 따라간 펜타곤에서 미 대통령의 묵인하에 놈들에 관한 정보를 얻었고, 함께하는 이들과 함께 사막을 피로 물들이며 위험이 될 만한 요소들을 잘라 냈다.
256|
257|납치한 아이들에게 사격 훈련을 시키는 반군 집단. 자살 테러까지 불사하는 광신도 테러리스트들…….
258|
259|앞을 막아서는 놈은 죽였고, 그렇게 죽은 놈들은 스켈레톤 킹의 언데드 군단에 복속되어 도망치는 놈들을 쫓았다.
260|

I remembered what Jeok Cheongang had told me just before I Logged Out: whether I’d wanted it or not, I’d drawn far more attention than I should have.

[P70]
The spotlight was bright. But everything around it was dark.

[P71]
I’d read that line in a novel I liked back in school. It was true. The brighter I became, the deeper the darkness around me grew.

[P72]
In Murim and in the modern world.

[P73]
“Team Leader Choi, are you saying…?”

[P74]
He understood the question and shook his head.

[P75]
“There’s been no major problem yet, but we’re facing pressure behind the scenes. We’ve put plans for more overseas branches on hold for now.”

[P76]
“It’s that serious?”

[P77]
“Every major Guild in the world is watching us. They don’t need to make a show of force to cause us trouble. If they decide to act, things won’t be easy for us.”

[P78]
“Why didn’t you tell me?”

[P79]
He gave me a flat look.

[P80]
“Did you give me a chance?”

[P81]
“…Fair.”

[P82]
This place was a fucking mess too.

[P83]
People with plenty to lose didn’t like the world changing. The handful of Hunters with mana cultivation methods of their own were no exception.

[P84]
*At this point, calling them power brokers would be more accurate than calling them Hunters.*

[P85]
Some of them might have enough influence to bend an entire country to their will. With their wealth, fame, and overwhelming strength, they could turn common sense on its head. They didn’t want change, and they certainly didn’t want anyone new rising to their level.

[P86]
Anyone like me or Team Leader Choi.

[P87]
*Even so, these bastards might be worse than Murim sects.*

[P88]
Leak a sect’s unique martial arts in Murim, and they’d hunt you down with murder in their eyes and smash your skull. But at least they wouldn’t throw a fit over a merchant selling the Three Calamities Sword Technique at a market.

[P89]
These guys already had more than enough, and they were ready to raise hell because we wanted to share one little mana cultivation method?

[P90]
*Huh. Now I’m pissed.*

[P91]
“If we release it, they’ll go nuts, right?”

[P92]
“Yes. And we’ll have a mess on our hands.”

[P93]
“What if I go after them?”

[P94]
“What?”

[P95]
“Now that I think about it, this is fucking ridiculous. We release the method without overthinking it, then I go after whichever assholes start trouble. That ought to shut them—”

[P96]
“No! Don’t! Absolutely not!”

[P97]
For Team Leader Choi’s normally low, composed voice to reach that volume, he might as well have said, *Over my dead body, you lunatic.*

[P98]
This time, though, I couldn’t just give in.

[P99]
“I know what you’re saying, Team Leader Choi, but we have to make it public. I didn’t create it to keep it to myself like a diary.”

[P100]
Magical power had already increased throughout the world. No—it was still increasing, even now. Mutation Gates were appearing one after another, and monster waves had begun.

[P101]
“Monsters are getting stronger as magical power increases. You know that. But if people learn this mana cultivation method now…”

[P102]
“Hunters’ abilities will improve across the board. It’s stable enough for even the lowest-ranked Hunters to learn without difficulty.”

[P103]
Team Leader Choi’s expression hardened.

[P104]
“I know what you’re thinking, Mr. Jin. That’s why you went after those rebel groups and terrorists in the first place, isn’t it? To reduce the chance of this method being misused.”

[P105]
“Yes. Before I worried about how sharp the weapon I’d made was, I had to think about whose hands it might end up in.”

[P106]
About two weeks ago in modern-world time, an incident in Texas had driven that point home: an attempted terrorist attack using a Magic Gem.

[P107]
Fortunately, the attempt had failed without any casualties. But it had made me realize something.

[P108]
“When I said I wanted to share it with *everyone*, that included every kind of criminal and lunatic.”

[P109]
Afterward, I followed Magic Johnson to the Pentagon. With the U.S. President’s tacit approval, we got intelligence on those people. Then my companions and I went into the desert, spilled a lot of blood, and cut down the threats we could find.

[P110]
Rebel groups that trained kidnapped children to shoot. Fanatical terrorists willing to carry out suicide attacks…

[P111]
I killed the ones who stood in our way. The dead joined the Skeleton King’s undead army and pursued those who fled.

[P112]
For the ones farther away, we used captured leaders to send false orders: rebel groups were told to attack terrorist organizations, and terrorist organizations were told to attack rebel groups.

[P113]
It was a war between bastards and motherfuckers. Tricked into launching all-out attacks on one another, both sides suffered massive losses.

[P114]
“As you know, we couldn’t wipe them out completely, and we won’t be able to in the future. But we’ve achieved what we needed to for now. Even if those bastards learn this method, they won’t be as dangerous as they were before.”

[P115]
They wouldn’t be the only ones growing stronger from it. Hunters everywhere would improve enough to fight monsters strengthened by the rise in magical power. That should help keep the balance.

[P116]
*And if things get much worse…*

[P117]
Then I’d release the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, too. So far, I’d taught it to only a handful of people, including Team Leader Choi.

[P118]
Low-ranking Hunters who knew nothing about mana cultivation methods couldn’t make use of it if I handed it to them now. But once they’d learned the basics, they could practice it on their own.

[P119]
I met Team Leader Choi’s eyes.

[P120]
“We have to make it public. One way or another.”

[P121]
“…”

[P122]
“Luckily, it isn’t too late. The public still thinks pretty highly of both of us.”

[P123]
“Pretty highly” was an understatement. People were going wild over us.

[P124]
I was being hailed as a young hero of a new age. After Butler Kim’s death, Team Leader Choi had become Guild Master of the Peace Guild—and before the paint on his new nameplate had dried, he’d taken over the Ares Guild too.

[P125]
Then there was the glow of his family name. His maternal grandfather was Cheon Taemin, the savior who had saved humanity from the Demon King Asmodeus. Team Leader Choi was his only blood relative and heir.

[P126]
I grabbed his hand.

[P127]
“Team Leader Choi.”

[P128]
I gripped it tight. When he met my fervent gaze, he flinched as though he’d been burned.

[P129]
“W-Why are you doing this all of a sudden?”

[P130]
He looked as though he’d run into Magic Johnson in a dark alley at night. I held on and pressed ahead.

[P131]
“If you’re that worried, let’s try another way. Hm?”

[P132]
“What way…?”

[P133]
“Let us use your grandfather’s name just this once.”

[P134]
“What?”

[P135]
“Come on. Let’s cash in on the savior’s name.”

[P136]
“…!”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P3]
Choi Minwoo watched the thought play out across Jin Taekyung’s face and let out an incredulous little laugh.

[P4]
*I really can’t figure him out.*

[P5]
Most of the time, his words, actions, and thoughts were as simple as could be. But every so often, Jin Taekyung showed a side of himself that went beyond surprising.

[P6]
*You’d think I’d be used to it by now. But this…*

[P7]
Choi Minwoo looked down at the table.

[P8]
**[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]**

[P9]
The crooked handwriting looked like a child’s, and the title was ridiculous. But there was nothing ridiculous about what filled those ten or so sheets of A4 paper.

[P10]
*He created an entirely new mana cultivation method.*

[P11]
There was a simple reason Choi Minwoo had teased him about his handwriting earlier. It was a small act of revenge for springing something this extraordinary on him without a word.

[P12]
The shock he had felt a few hours ago had been that great.

[P13]
*How is this possible?*

[P14]
He had never seen explanations or instructions so simple and clear. The method was exceptionally stable, with a firm grounding in the fundamentals.

[P15]
Choi Minwoo had grown skilled enough to hold his own against a Peak master of Murim. He had recognized the value of this new method immediately. He had also understood what the recent events that had drawn the world’s attention meant to Jin Taekyung.

[P16]
“The Week of Judgment.”

[P17]
Choi Minwoo broke the brief silence and looked at Jin Taekyung.

[P18]
“‘Just as God created heaven and earth over the course of a week, terrorists around the world endured a Week of Judgment.’ President Doramp Jr. said that at a White House press conference a few days ago.”

[P19]
The President of the United States had said it in public. Naturally, his provocative remarks had spread around the world in less than an hour. By now, everyone in Korea had heard about them.

[P20]
Everyone but one person, perhaps.

[P21]
“He said that?”

[P22]
Jin Taekyung had been holed up in the training room the whole time. Choi Minwoo nodded.

[P23]
“It was a fairly aggressive thing for any president to say, especially the American president. Some people criticized him for deliberately provoking the terrorists.”

[P24]
“Hm. Why bring up something as grand as the creation of heaven and earth? Were there any retaliatory attacks?”

[P25]
“None. Not a single one.”

[P26]
“Not one?”

[P27]
“No. If anything, they’ve been keeping their mouths shut.”

[P28]
The sullen look on Jin Taekyung’s face eased a little.

[P29]
“Guess beating the crap out of them paid off.”

[P30]
Choi Minwoo studied him for a moment, then spoke.

[P31]
“So that was why.”

[P32]
“Why what?”

[P33]
“I’ve been thinking about two things. Why you suddenly went after the terrorists, and why you gave me this new mana cultivation method.”

[P34]
Now he had his answer.

[P35]
**[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]**

[P36]
Choi Minwoo lifted the papers, held together with a single careless staple.

[P37]
“You’re planning to make this mana cultivation method available to everyone.”

[P38]
Jin Taekyung grinned.

[P39]
“Our Team Leader Choi really is sharp.”

[P40]
* * *

[P41]
The look Team Leader Choi gave me was hard to read. Part of it seemed like admiration. The rest looked like he had a lot to think about.

[P42]
“Why? Is there a problem?”

[P43]
“Well…”

[P44]
He ran a hand through his disheveled hair.

[P45]
“There are so many problems, I don’t know where to start.”

[P46]
“There’s nothing wrong with the mana cultivation method itself, so you mean practical problems.”

[P47]
“…Yes. Unfortunately.”

[P48]
“What’s the biggest one?”

[P49]
He thought for a moment.

[P50]
“For starters, making the method public is a problem in its own right.”

[P51]
“Go on.”

[P52]
“You know that only a tiny fraction of high-ranking Hunters possess mana cultivation methods. They’re closely guarded knowledge—secret arts, essentially. You also know how closed-off those Hunters are, and how different their world is from the one other Hunters live in.”

[P53]
“I know. I’ve been in this business for years. Though back when I was an F-rank Hunter, I’d never even heard of a mana cultivation method.”

[P54]
No profession divided its members more sharply than the Hunter business.

[P55]
Ordinary people judged one another by education, family background, and looks. Hunters were sorted into high and low by rank alone.

[P56]
How much mana you’d been granted. How agile you were. How strong. Those crude measures determined your place, and you were graded like cattle headed for slaughter.

[P57]
*There’s a reason they call F-rank Hunters slaves.*

[P58]
High-ranking Hunters, meanwhile, practically lived above the clouds. They earned more from a single raid than most Hunters could make in a lifetime and spent their days under spotlights and envious stares.

[P59]
Maybe that was why they’d built walls around themselves, like nobles of old living inside their castles. No one but another high-ranking Hunter could cross those walls. Even if someone was lucky enough to receive a high rank, the gate opened only with their permission.

[P60]
Those high-ranking Hunters were connected by invisible ties across the world, each protected by the giant Guild they belonged to.

[P61]
“This isn’t limited to Korea,” Team Leader Choi said. “If you make this method public, the backlash will be greater than you expect.”

[P62]
“Because they’ll think releasing a mana cultivation method makes what they have less valuable?”

[P63]
“That’s part of it. There’s another reason.”

[P64]
“What?”

[P65]
“The problem is that it’s *us*.”

[P66]
“…!”

[P67]
That brief answer was enough.

[P68]
*Have we stood out too much?*

[P69]
I remembered what Jeok Cheongang had told me just before I Logged Out: whether I’d wanted it or not, I’d drawn far more attention than I should have.

[P70]
The spotlight was bright. But everything around it was dark.

[P71]
I’d read that line in a novel I liked back in school. It was true. The brighter I became, the deeper the darkness around me grew.

[P72]
In Murim and in the modern world.

[P73]
“Team Leader Choi, are you saying…?”

[P74]
He understood the question and shook his head.

[P75]
“There’s been no major problem yet, but we’re facing pressure behind the scenes. We’ve put plans for more overseas branches on hold for now.”

[P76]
“It’s that serious?”

[P77]
“Every major Guild in the world is watching us. They don’t need to make a show of force to cause us trouble. If they decide to act, things won’t be easy for us.”

[P78]
“Why didn’t you tell me?”

[P79]
He gave me a flat look.

[P80]
“Did you give me a chance?”

[P81]
“…Fair.”

[P82]
This place was a fucking mess too.

[P83]
People with plenty to lose didn’t like the world changing. The handful of Hunters with mana cultivation methods of their own were no exception.

[P84]
*At this point, calling them power brokers would be more accurate than calling them Hunters.*

[P85]
Some of them might have enough influence to bend an entire country to their will. With their wealth, fame, and overwhelming strength, they could turn common sense on its head. They didn’t want change, and they certainly didn’t want anyone new rising to their level.

[P86]
Anyone like me or Team Leader Choi.

[P87]
*Even so, these bastards might be worse than Murim sects.*

[P88]
Leak a sect’s unique martial arts in Murim, and they’d hunt you down with murder in their eyes and smash your skull. But at least they wouldn’t throw a fit over a merchant selling the Three Calamities Sword Technique at a market.

[P89]
These guys already had more than enough, and they were ready to raise hell because we wanted to share one little mana cultivation method?

[P90]
*Huh. Now I’m pissed.*

[P91]
“If we release it, they’ll go nuts, right?”

[P92]
“Yes. And we’ll have a mess on our hands.”

[P93]
“What if I go after them?”

[P94]
“What?”

[P95]
“Now that I think about it, this is fucking ridiculous. We release the method without overthinking it, then I go after whichever assholes start trouble. That ought to shut them—”

[P96]
“No! Don’t! Absolutely not!”

[P97]
For Team Leader Choi’s normally low, composed voice to reach that volume, he might as well have said, *Over my dead body, you lunatic.*

[P98]
This time, though, I couldn’t just give in.

[P99]
“I know what you’re saying, Team Leader Choi, but we have to make it public. I didn’t create it to keep it to myself like a diary.”

[P100]
Magical power had already increased throughout the world. No—it was still increasing, even now. Mutation Gates were appearing one after another, and monster waves had begun.

[P101]
“Monsters are getting stronger as magical power increases. You know that. But if people learn this mana cultivation method now…”

[P102]
“Hunters’ abilities will improve across the board. It’s stable enough for even the lowest-ranked Hunters to learn without difficulty.”

[P103]
Team Leader Choi’s expression hardened.

[P104]
“I know what you’re thinking, Mr. Jin. That’s why you went after those rebel groups and terrorists in the first place, isn’t it? To reduce the chance of this method being misused.”

[P105]
“Yes. Before I worried about how sharp the weapon I’d made was, I had to think about whose hands it might end up in.”

[P106]
About two weeks ago in modern-world time, an incident in Texas had driven that point home: an attempted terrorist attack using a Magic Gem.

[P107]
Fortunately, the attempt had failed without any casualties. But it had made me realize something.

[P108]
“When I said I wanted to share it with *everyone*, that included every kind of criminal and lunatic.”

[P109]
Afterward, I followed Magic Johnson to the Pentagon. With the U.S. President’s tacit approval, we got intelligence on those people. Then my companions and I went into the desert, spilled a lot of blood, and cut down the threats we could find.

[P110]
Rebel groups that trained kidnapped children to shoot. Fanatical terrorists willing to carry out suicide attacks…

[P111]
I killed the ones who stood in our way. The dead joined the Skeleton King’s undead army and pursued those who fled.

[P112]
For the ones farther away, we used captured leaders to send false orders: rebel groups were told to attack terrorist organizations, and terrorist organizations were told to attack rebel groups.

[P113]
It was a war between bastards and motherfuckers. Tricked into launching all-out attacks on one another, both sides suffered massive losses.

[P114]
“As you know, we couldn’t wipe them out completely, and we won’t be able to in the future. But we’ve achieved what we needed to for now. Even if those bastards learn this method, they won’t be as dangerous as they were before.”

[P115]
They wouldn’t be the only ones growing stronger from it. Hunters everywhere would improve enough to fight monsters strengthened by the rise in magical power. That should help keep the balance.

[P116]
*And if things get much worse…*

[P117]
Then I’d release the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, too. So far, I’d taught it to only a handful of people, including Team Leader Choi.

[P118]
Low-ranking Hunters who knew nothing about mana cultivation methods couldn’t make use of it if I handed it to them now. But once they’d learned the basics, they could practice it on their own.

[P119]
I met Team Leader Choi’s eyes.

[P120]
“We have to make it public. One way or another.”

[P121]
“…”

[P122]
“Luckily, it isn’t too late. The public still thinks pretty highly of both of us.”

[P123]
“Pretty highly” was an understatement. People were going wild over us.

[P124]
I was being hailed as a young hero of a new age. After Butler Kim’s death, Team Leader Choi had become Guild Master of the Peace Guild—and before the paint on his new nameplate had dried, he’d taken over the Ares Guild too.

[P125]
Then there was the glow of his family name. His maternal grandfather was Cheon Taemin, the savior who had saved humanity from the Demon King Asmodeus. Team Leader Choi was his only blood relative and heir.

[P126]
I grabbed his hand.

[P127]
“Team Leader Choi.”

[P128]
I gripped it tight. When he met my fervent gaze, he flinched as though he’d been burned.

[P129]
“W-Why are you doing this all of a sudden?”

[P130]
He looked as though he’d run into Magic Johnson in a dark alley at night. I held on and pressed ahead.

[P131]
“If you’re that worried, let’s try another way. Hm?”

[P132]
“What way…?”

[P133]
“Let us use your grandfather’s name just this once.”

[P134]
“What?”

[P135]
“Come on. Let’s cash in on the savior’s name.”

[P136]
“…!”

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.

“Why? Is there a problem?”

[P43]
“Well…”

[P44]
He ran a hand through his disheveled hair.

[P45]
“There are so many problems, I don’t know where to start.”

[P46]
“There’s nothing wrong with the mana cultivation method itself, so you mean practical problems.”

[P47]
“…Yes. Unfortunately.”

[P48]
“What’s the biggest one?”

[P49]
He thought for a moment.

[P50]
“For starters, making the method public is a problem in its own right.”

[P51]
“Go on.”

[P52]
“You know that only a tiny fraction of high-ranking Hunters possess mana cultivation methods. They’re closely guarded knowledge—secret arts, essentially. You also know how closed-off those Hunters are, and how different their world is from the one other Hunters live in.”

[P53]
“I know. I’ve been in this business for years. Though back when I was an F-rank Hunter, I’d never even heard of a mana cultivation method.”

[P54]
No profession divided its members more sharply than the Hunter business.

[P55]
Ordinary people judged one another by education, family background, and looks. Hunters were sorted into high and low by rank alone.

[P56]
How much mana you’d been granted. How agile you were. How strong. Those crude measures determined your place, and you were graded like cattle headed for slaughter.

[P57]
*There’s a reason they call F-rank Hunters slaves.*

[P58]
High-ranking Hunters, meanwhile, practically lived above the clouds. They earned more from a single raid than most Hunters could make in a lifetime and spent their days under spotlights and envious stares.

[P59]
Maybe that was why they’d built walls around themselves, like nobles of old living inside their castles. No one but another high-ranking Hunter could cross those walls. Even if someone was lucky enough to receive a high rank, the gate opened only with their permission.

[P60]
Those high-ranking Hunters were connected by invisible ties across the world, each protected by the giant Guild they belonged to.

[P61]
“This isn’t limited to Korea,” Team Leader Choi said. “If you make this method public, the backlash will be greater than you expect.”

[P62]
“Because they’ll think releasing a mana cultivation method makes what they have less valuable?”

[P63]
“That’s part of it. There’s another reason.”

[P64]
“What?”

[P65]
“The problem is that it’s *us*.”

[P66]
“…!”

[P67]
That brief answer was enough.

[P68]
*Have we stood out too much?*

[P69]
I remembered what Jeok Cheongang had told me just before I Logged Out: whether I’d wanted it or not, I’d drawn far more attention than I should have.

[P70]
The spotlight was bright. But everything around it was dark.

[P71]
I’d read that line in a novel I liked back in school. It was true. The brighter I became, the deeper the darkness around me grew.

[P72]
In Murim and in the modern world.

[P73]
“Team Leader Choi, are you saying…?”

[P74]
He understood the question and shook his head.

[P75]
“There’s been no major problem yet, but we’re facing pressure behind the scenes. We’ve put plans for more overseas branches on hold for now.”

[P76]
“It’s that serious?”

[P77]
“Every major Guild in the world is watching us. They don’t need to make a show of force to cause us trouble. If they decide to act, things won’t be easy for us.”

[P78]
“Why didn’t you tell me?”

[P79]
He gave me a flat look.

[P80]
“Did you give me a chance?”

[P81]
“…Fair.”

[P82]
This place was a fucking mess too.

[P83]
People with plenty to lose didn’t like the world changing. The handful of Hunters with mana cultivation methods of their own were no exception.

[P84]
*At this point, calling them power brokers would be more accurate than calling them Hunters.*

[P85]
Some of them might have enough influence to bend an entire country to their will. With their wealth, fame, and overwhelming strength, they could turn common sense on its head. They didn’t want change, and they certainly didn’t want anyone new rising to their level.

[P86]
Anyone like me or Team Leader Choi.

[P87]
*Even so, these bastards might be worse than Murim sects.*

[P88]
Leak a sect’s unique martial arts in Murim, and they’d hunt you down with murder in their eyes and smash your skull. But at least they wouldn’t throw a fit over a merchant selling the Three Calamities Sword Technique at a market.

[P89]
These guys already had more than enough, and they were ready to raise hell because we wanted to share one little mana cultivation method?

[P90]
*Huh. Now I’m pissed.*

[P91]
“If we release it, they’ll go nuts, right?”

[P92]
“Yes. And we’ll have a mess on our hands.”

[P93]
“What if I go after them?”

[P94]
“What?”

[P95]
“Now that I think about it, this is fucking ridiculous. We release the method without overthinking it, then I go after whichever assholes start trouble. That ought to shut them—”

[P96]
“No! Don’t! Absolutely not!”

[P97]
For Team Leader Choi’s normally low, composed voice to reach that volume, he might as well have said, *Over my dead body, you lunatic.*

[P98]
This time, though, I couldn’t just give in.

[P99]
“I know what you’re saying, Team Leader Choi, but we have to make it public. I didn’t create it to keep it to myself like a diary.”

[P100]
Magical power had already increased throughout the world. No—it was still increasing, even now. Mutation Gates were appearing one after another, and monster waves had begun.

[P101]
“Monsters are getting stronger as magical power increases. You know that. But if people learn this mana cultivation method now…”

[P102]
“Hunters’ abilities will improve across the board. It’s stable enough for even the lowest-ranked Hunters to learn without difficulty.”

[P103]
Team Leader Choi’s expression hardened.

[P104]
“I know what you’re thinking, Mr. Jin. That’s why you went after those rebel groups and terrorists in the first place, isn’t it? To reduce the chance of this method being misused.”

[P105]
“Yes. Before I worried about how sharp the weapon I’d made was, I had to think about whose hands it might end up in.”

[P106]
About two weeks ago in modern-world time, an incident in Texas had driven that point home: an attempted terrorist attack using a Magic Gem.

[P107]
Fortunately, the attempt had failed without any casualties. But it had made me realize something.

[P108]
“When I said I wanted to share it with *everyone*, that included every kind of criminal and lunatic.”

[P109]
Afterward, I followed Magic Johnson to the Pentagon. With the U.S. President’s tacit approval, we got intelligence on those people. Then my companions and I went into the desert, spilled a lot of blood, and cut down the threats we could find.

[P110]
Rebel groups that trained kidnapped children to shoot. Fanatical terrorists willing to carry out suicide attacks…

[P111]
I killed the ones who stood in our way. The dead joined the Skeleton King’s undead army and pursued those who fled.

[P112]
For the ones farther away, we used captured leaders to send false orders: rebel groups were told to attack terrorist organizations, and terrorist organizations were told to attack rebel groups.

[P113]
It was a war between bastards and motherfuckers. Tricked into launching all-out attacks on one another, both sides suffered massive losses.

[P114]
“As you know, we couldn’t wipe them out completely, and we won’t be able to in the future. But we’ve achieved what we needed to for now. Even if those bastards learn this method, they won’t be as dangerous as they were before.”

[P115]
They wouldn’t be the only ones growing stronger from it. Hunters everywhere would improve enough to fight monsters strengthened by the rise in magical power. That should help keep the balance.

[P116]
*And if things get much worse…*

[P117]
Then I’d release the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, too. So far, I’d taught it to only a handful of people, including Team Leader Choi.

[P118]
Low-ranking Hunters who knew nothing about mana cultivation methods couldn’t make use of it if I handed it to them now. But once they’d learned the basics, they could practice it on their own.

[P119]
I met Team Leader Choi’s eyes.

[P120]
“We have to make it public. One way or another.”

[P121]
“…”

[P122]
“Luckily, it isn’t too late. The public still thinks pretty highly of both of us.”

[P123]
“Pretty highly” was an understatement. People were going wild over us.

[P124]
I was being hailed as a young hero of a new age. After Butler Kim’s death, Team Leader Choi had become Guild Master of the Peace Guild—and before the paint on his new nameplate had dried, he’d taken over the Ares Guild too.

[P125]
Then there was the glow of his family name. His maternal grandfather was Cheon Taemin, the savior who had saved humanity from the Demon King Asmodeus. Team Leader Choi was his only blood relative and heir.

[P126]
I grabbed his hand.

[P127]
“Team Leader Choi.”

[P128]
I gripped it tight. When he met my fervent gaze, he flinched as though he’d been burned.

[P129]
“W-Why are you doing this all of a sudden?”

[P130]
He looked as though he’d run into Magic Johnson in a dark alley at night. I held on and pressed ahead.

[P131]
“If you’re that worried, let’s try another way. Hm?”

[P132]
“What way…?”

[P133]
“Let us use your grandfather’s name just this once.”

[P134]
“What?”

[P135]
“Come on. Let’s cash in on the savior’s name.”

[P136]
“…!”

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
